data.title: Canada’s MTY Food Group Raises Dividend 35% as Profits Accelerate
data.description:
Canada’s MTY Food Group ($TSE: MTY) has raised its dividend an impressive 35%. The Montreal-based company operates restaurant chains across North America, with most locations found in shopping mall food courts. Brands operated by MTY Food Group include Thai Express, Extreme Pita, Taco Time, and Yogen Früz.

Going forward, MTY Food Group said that it will pay shareholders a quarterly distribution of C$0.50 per share (US$0.35). That’s up 35% from a previous dividend payment per quarter of C$0.37. data.title: Verizon (VZ) Stock: Is That 6.6% Yield Worth the Risk?

data.title: Bank of America Fined $1.2 Billion for Money Laundering Failures Ahead of Q3 Results
data.description:
Bank of America (BAC) is facing a $1.21 billion penalty from U.S. regulators over anti-money laundering and sanctions compliance failures. Following the news, BAC shares fell 2.3% in extended trading on Tuesday. The penalty has put the spotlight on the bank ahead of its third-quarter 2026 earnings report due before the market opens today, October 14.

Regulators said Bank of America failed to properly monitor transactions, check customer information, and identify suspicious activity, relying too heavily on external inquiries instead of its own controls.

The bank acknowledged the violations and said it had invested billions of dollars in technology and assigned thousands of employees to combat financial crime.

Here’s What Happened

The U.S. Department of the Treasury announced the penalty on October 13, citing the bank’s failure to identify and report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions. These included activities potentially linked to Chinese money laundering networks, fraud, and illicit financing along the U.S. southwest border.

The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) assessed a $1.2 billion penalty. Meanwhile, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) imposed a $750 million civil penalty, the largest in the regulator’s history. The OCC penalty will be credited toward FinCEN’s assessment. Separately, the Office of Foreign Assets Control reached an $11.6 million settlement with the bank over apparent sanctions violations involving countries including Russia and Iran.

What Does the Fine Mean for BAC Stock?

The penalty is expected to weigh on Bank of America’s third-quarter results. The bank said the $1.2 billion charge will be non-tax-deductible and reduce net income by approximately $0.17 per share.

Analysts had expected earnings of $1.10 per share and revenue of approximately $30.69 billion before accounting for the penalty. Analysts will watch how the charge affects earnings and whether management provides more details on compliance costs.

Furthermore, investors will assess the bank’s underlying business performance, management’s remediation plans, and any impact on shareholder returns. BAC currently pays a regular quarterly dividend of $0.32 per share, reflecting a yield of 2.13%. While the fine creates uncertainty, it does not directly limit the bank’s ability to grow its lending business.

Is BAC a Good Buy Right Now?

On TipRanks, BAC has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 13 Buys and three Hold ratings. The average Bank of America price target of $65.87 implies 22.1% upside potential from current levels.

data.title: Johnson & Johnson Stock Falls Despite Beating Q3 Expectations – Here’s Why
data.description:
Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) reported better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results on Tuesday, driven by strong pharmaceutical sales. However, JNJ stock fell in premarket trading as slower growth in its medical technology business and concerns about international sales weighed on investor sentiment.

The healthcare giant posted revenue of $25.40 billion, topping analysts’ expectations of $25.28 billion. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.59 per share, above the consensus estimate of $2.53. However, diluted earnings per share of $0.09 included one-time costs related to the talc lawsuit settlement, the Firefly Bio acquisition, and a partnership with Sail Biomedicines.

Despite these challenges, JNJ raised its 2026 forecast. The company now expects sales of about $101.2 billion and adjusted earnings of $11.10 per share, up from its earlier estimates of $101.1 billion and $11.04, respectively.

Pharmaceutical Sales Drive Growth but Medtech Suffers

JNJ’s pharmaceutical division sales rose 7.7% year-over-year to $16.76 billion. Tremfya was a key growth driver, with sales surging 68.3% to $2.39 billion. The drug is helping offset declining revenue from Stelara, which faces generic competition. Stelara sales fell 54.4% to $716 million. Meanwhile, sales of blood cancer treatment Darzalex increased 15.4% to $4.24 billion.

The medical technology division delivered weaker growth, with sales increasing just 2.5% to $8.64 billion. International sales remained weak due to Middle East tensions, spending cuts in Europe, and pricing pressure in China.

Additionally, sales of Abiomed’s Impella heart pumps remained weak after a UK study raised concerns about their use in certain high-risk heart procedures.

Chief Financial Officer Joe Wolk said the Middle East conflict has affected regional sales as governments redirect spending toward defense, noting that their “budgets now are being resourced and allocated towards defense.”

data.title: Nike (NKE) Defends Its Dividend as Company Restructures
data.description:
Nike (NKE) is defending its dividend payment as its finance deteriorate and it undertakes a restructuring of its operations meant to cut costs and conserve cash. Currently, Nike pays a quarterly distribution to stockholders of $0.41 per share. That gives the slumping stock a yield of nearly 5%, one of the highest payouts among the 30 constituents in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

Some analysts have suggested that the sneaker giant could cut its dividend to help conserve cash and give the company money needed to help fund its ongoing turnaround strategy. However, management defended the dividend on their most recent earnings call with analysts and media, saying the distribution is safe for now.

data.title: McDonald’s Stock (MCD) Looks Like a Buy after the Dip
data.description:
McDonald’s (MCD) stock’s current dip looks increasingly attractive, and I see MCD as a Buy. For a mature, low-beta business known for steady cash flow, this kind of sell-off is unusual. MCD rarely offers investors many dramatic entry points, but the setup looks very different after it fell more than 30% from its peak earlier this year.

The recent sell-off reflects real and plausible concerns. Affordability remains the biggest problem for the fast-food bellwether, and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) drugs add a new long-term risk. Still, most of the current pressure looks more cyclical than structural. At the same time, the drop makes MCD much cheaper and pushes the dividend yield higher. NEXT also gives management a clear plan to improve restaurant economics and recover traffic.

data.title: Accenture Stock (ACN) Is Recovering, but Q4 Earnings Could Decide What Comes Next
data.description:
Accenture (ACN) stock is recovering and seems to have finally emerged from “falling knife” mode. After falling nearly 60% from its January peak and dipping close to $118 after a disappointing Q3, the Dublin, Ireland-based consulting firm has already recovered nearly 50% from its lows. Accenture’s next test will be crucial — its Q4 earnings, scheduled for October 1 before the opening bell.

Part of the recovery was because the market began to realize it may have overreacted by treating the company as a structural victim of artificial intelligence (AI). Moreover, Consulting, its core business, remains weak. Bookings need to pick up, and FY27 guidance could determine whether this rerating has more room to run.

My thesis is that the recovery can continue, but the upside is no longer as attractive as it was a few months ago. I remain constructive and still see ACN as a Buy, though not quite the Strong Buy it looked like before Q3.

data.title: Caterpillar Stock (CAT) Pullback Could Offer a Strong Entry Point
data.description:
Caterpillar (CAT) stock’s pullback could offer a strong entry point, in my view. This is because the global construction equipment manufacturer is becoming less dependent on any single industrial upswing. Today, shares sit about 23.5% below June’s record high. However, Caterpillar exited Q2 with a record $72 billion backlog, marking a 92% year-over-year increase.

CEO Joe Creed said, “Strong order rates and a growing backlog reflect broadening momentum across all three of our primary segments.” The valuation asks the company to execute strongly ahead, but today’s demand mix looks longer-lived than the market’s old cyclical framing. Thus, my CAT stock forecast is bullish.
